newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA GIVE KNOX SURPRISE RECALL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA GIVE KNOX SURPRISE RECALL.

text.p: Australia on Monday recalled veteran fly-half David Knox to their squad for this weekend's Tri-Nations rugby union test against South Africa in a remarkable change of heart by coach Greg Smith.

Knox will interrupt a playing stint with South African province Natal to join the Wallabies in Brisbane for Saturday's test as a replacement for injured Tim Horan, the Australian Rugby Union (ARU) said on Monday.
Smith has persistently ignored Knox this season, preferring to switch Horan from centre despite a near-total lack of previous experience in the specialist fly-half position.
Wallaby full-back Matt Burke will also be missing against South Africa after suffering a recurrence of a groin injury.
Australia will make at least one other change from the side that lost 33-18 against New Zealand in a Tri-Nations test in Melbourne on Saturday after dropping number eight Michael Brial.
The back rower was singled out by Smith for blame after the All Blacks demolished the Wallabies to lift the Bledisloe Cup in front of a 90,000 crowd at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Veteran Troy Coker was expected to replace Brial while Stephen Larkham will almost certainly come into the side at full-back.
After making public some team details, including Knox's recall, the ARU delayed announcing the full squad until later on Monday.
Horan broke his hand during the first half against the All Blacks and will be out of action for more than one month.
In justiying his previous selection decisions, Smith has repeatedly argued that Knox's acknowledged attacking talent does not compensate for his poor defensive ability.
Even in the aftermath of the Wallabies' defeat on Saturday, Smith stressed that he had no plans at that stage to recall Knox from South Africa.
In Monday's The Australian newspaper, Smith was quoted as saying that Knox represented too much of a risk. "He's a non-tackler," Smith told the newspaper.
Smith, under intense pressure to keep his job next season, pinned his tactics this year on Horan's strength at running with the ball.
But the policy caused widespread misgiving, with critics questioning Horan's suitability by citing concerns about the slow speed of his passing and the lack of a kicking game.
Knox, 33, a proven goal-kicker, enjoyed an outstanding season for ACT Brumbies in the Super 12 competition, helping the province to a losing final against Auckland in March.
When Smith opted for Horan for earlier home test matches against France, Knox signed to play Natal in the domestic Currie Cup competition.
Knox, who launched a scathing attack on Australia's selection policy before his departurne, will leave South Africa late on Monday night, the ARU said.
Both South Africa and Australia lost to New Zealand in their opening Tri-Nations matches.
